ὅτε παραδεξάμενοι, ἐπετελοῦντο σαρκὶ, καθάπερ ἀμέλει καὶ τῶν ἐν Γαλατίᾳ τινὲς, οἷς
καὶ ὁ θεσπέσιος Παῦλος ἐπιπλήττει λέγων "Ἐναρξάμενοι πνεύματι νῦν σαρκὶ

9

ἐπιτελεῖσθε;" ἔδει τοίνυν σαφεῖ καὶ ἐναργεστάτῳ κηρύγματι τῆς ἀληθείας αὐτοῖς
ἀνευρῦναι τὴν ὁδὸν, καὶ ὡς ἡ περιτομὴ οὐδέν ἐστι τῶν ἄλλων ἐντολῶν τοῦ Θεοῦ
ἐστερημένη· ὁμοίως δὲ καὶ ἡ ἀκροβυστία οὐδέν ἐστι μὴ εὐαγγελικῷ βίῳ κεκοσμημένη.
Προσήκει τοίνυν τὸν κεκλημένον ἐν τῇ κλήσει μένειν ὅπως ἂν ἔχοι σχήματος· μέτεισι
δὲ ἀναγκαίως ἐπὶ τὸ χρῆναι πάλιν δυσφημίαν ἑτέραν μονονουχὶ ἀποσοβεῖν τοῦ θείου
κηρύγματος· πνεῦμα μὲν γὰρ δουλείας ἦν ἐν τοῖς ὑπὸ νόμον· τὸ δὲ θέσπισμα τὸ
εὐαγγελικὸν, τῆς υἱοθεσίας τὸ πνεῦμα τοῖς πιστεύειν ἐθέλουσιν ἐνίεσθαί φησιν, καὶ οὐκ
ἔτι καλοῦν εἰς δουλείαν, ἀλλ' εἰς ἐλεύθερον ἀξίωμα.

ΤΟΥ ΑΥΤΟΥ ΕΚ ΤΟΥ ∆ ΤΟΜΟΥ ΤΗΣ ΠΡΟΣ ΚΟΡΙΝΘΙΟΥΣ ΚΥΡΙΛΛΟΥ.
∆οῦλος ἐκλήθης; μή σοι μελέτω. ἘΠΕΙ∆Η τινες τῆς τοῦ Ἁγίου Πνεύματος
ἀξιούμενοι χάριτος, τὸν τῆς κατὰ σάρκα δουλείας ἀπεσείοντο ζυγὸν, ἐπιστέλλει μὲν καὶ
δι' ἑτέρων "Μόνον μὴ τὴν ἐλευθερίαν εἰς "ἀφορμὴν τῇ σαρκὶ," καταγοητεύει δὲ ὥσπερ
καὶ διὰ τούτων αὐτοὺς ἀστειότατα λέγων ∆οῦλος ἐκλήθης; μή σοι μελέτω· ἀλλ' εἰ καὶ
δύνασαι ἐλεύθερος γενέσθαι, μᾶλλον χρῆσαι· τουτέστι κἂν εἰς τὸν τῆς δουλείας τῆς
κατὰ σάρκα ζυγὸν ἐπηρτημένον ἔχων ἐκλήθης διὰ τῆς πίστεως εἰς ἐλευθέραν υἱότητα,
κἂν εἰ τῆς θείας φύσεως γέγονας κοινωνὸς, ἄμεινον ἔσο μικροψυχίας, οὐκ ἄμισθον
εὑρήσεις τὸν ἐπὶ τῇ δουλείᾳ πόνον· οἶδεν μὲν γὰρ ἐλευθέραν τὴν φύσιν ὁ δημιουργός·
πεποίηται γὰρ οὕτως παρ' αὐτοῦ· πλεονεξία δέ τις παρεισδραμοῦσά πως κατὰ καιροὺς
τῷ τῆς ἐλευθερίας κάλλει διελυμήνατο. δεῖ δὲ δὴ πάντως τοὺς πεπονθότας, ἀποφορτί
274 σασθαι τὸ κακὸν, μεταστοιχειοῦντος ἅπαντα πρὸς τὸ ἐν ἀρχαῖς τοῦ Χριστοῦ· καινὴ
γὰρ κτίσις τὰ ἐν αὐτῷ καὶ οὔτε δοῦλος οὔτε "ἐλεύθερος ἀλλὰ τὰ πάντα καὶ ἐν πᾶσιν"
αὐτός. καὶ γοῦν ὁ Ἡσαΐας τοῦ προσδοκωμένου καὶ τοῦ μέλλοντος ἔσεσθαι βίου τὴν
κατάστασιν καὶ τὴν ἰσότητα τὴν παρὰ Θεῷ προανακέκραγεν λέγων "Καὶ ἔσται ὁ λαὸς ὡς
"ὁ ἱερεὺς, καὶ ὁ παῖς ὡς ὁ κύριος, καὶ ἡ θεράπαινα ὡς ἡ "κυρία." οὐκοῦν κἂν εἰ δύναιό
φησιν ἐλεύθερος γενέσθαι, μᾶλλον χρῆσαι· καὶ γάρ ἐστιν, ὡς ἔφην, οὐκ ἀκερδὴς ὁ ζυγὸς
τοῖς ἀγαθῇ κεχρημένοις εὐνοίᾳ καὶ ὀρθῶς ἐν αὐτῷ διαγεγονόσιν· ἀδικήσει δὲ τὸ σύμπαν
οὐδὲν τὸ νῦν ἐκ πλεονεξίας ἐπεῤῥίφθαι τισὶ τὴν κατὰ σάρκα δουλείαν, ἔσται ἂν ἅπασιν
ἐν ἴσῳ τρόπῳ καὶ λόγῳ σώζηται τὸ ἐλεύθερον παρά γε τῷ τὰ δίκαια κρίνοντι καὶ τὰ καθ'
ἡμᾶς ὁσίως ταλαντεύοντι Θεῷ. ἄλλως τε, φησὶν, οὐκ ἂν εἴη τῶν ἐνδεχομένων
ἀνθρώπους ὄντας ἡμᾶς τὸ τῆς δουλείας ὄνομα φυγεῖν· δοῦλον γὰρ ἅπαν ἐστὶ τὸ
πεποιημένον καὶ τοῖς θείοις ὑποφέρεται σκήπτροις πᾶν ὅπερ ἐστὶ κεκλημένον εἰς
γένεσιν· ὥστε καὶ ὁ δοῦλος ἀπελεύθερός ἐστι Χριστοῦ, δοῦλος δὲ πάντως καὶ ὁ
κεκλημένος εἰς ἐλευθερίαν, καθά φησιν ὁ ψαλμός "ὅτι τὰ "σύμπαντα δοῦλα σά."
Ἀποφαίνει γεμὴν ὁ μυσταγωγὸς καὶ καθ' ἕτερον τρόπον ὠφελουμένους Χριστῷ
τοὺς δι' αὐτὸν σεσωσμένους· ταύτῃ τοί φησι Τιμῆς ἠγοράσθητε, μὴ γίνεσθε δοῦλοι
ἀνθρώπων· ἠγοράσμεθα μὲν γὰρ τιμῆς ὁμολογουμένως τεθεικότος ὑπὲρ 275 ἡμῶν τὸ
ἴδιον αἷμα τοῦ πάντων ἡμῶν Σωτῆρος Χριστοῦ, ἐξῃρήμεθα δὲ τῆς τοῦ διαβόλου
πλεονεξίας, τῆς τῶν δαιμονίων ὠμότητος, κεκλήμεθα δὲ πρὸς ἐλευθερίαν διὰ Χριστοῦ.
οὐκοῦν ὡς ἠγορασμένοι καὶ τῷ πριαμένῳ τὴν ἑαυτῶν ὀφείλοντες ζωὴν, μὴ γίνεσθέ
φησι δοῦλοι ἀνθρώπων. καὶ οὔτι φαμὲν ὡς τῆς κατὰ σάρκα δουλείας ἀποπηδᾶν
ἀναπείθει, διδάσκει δὲ μᾶλλον ἐκεῖνο καὶ μάλα ὀρθῶς μὴ δουλεύειν τοῖς ἀποφέρειν
pass_a_gloss: [Sentence continues from u03-open: ‘although the faith sometimes (ἔσθ’ ὅτε)’] having received (παραδεξάμενοι), they were being completed (ἐπετελοῦντο) in flesh (σαρκί), just as indeed some of those in Galatia, whom the divine (θεσπέσιος) Paul rebukes (ἐπιπλήττει) saying ‘Having begun (ἐναρξάμενοι) in spirit, now in flesh are you being completed?’ It was needed therefore by clear and most vivid proclamation (κήρυγμα) of the truth to widen (ἀνευρῦναι) the road for them, and that circumcision (περιτομή) is nothing deprived of the other commandments (ἐντολαί) of God; likewise also foreskin (ἀκροβυστία) is nothing not adorned with gospel life (εὐαγγελικῷ βίῳ). It befits therefore the one called to remain in the calling (κλῆσις) of whatever form (σχῆμα) he has. He passes (μέτεισι) necessarily to needing again to all but (μονονουχί) scare off (ἀποσοβεῖν) another slander (δυσφημία) of the divine proclamation; for a spirit of slavery (δουλεία) was in those under law; but the gospel decree (θέσπισμα) says the spirit of adoption (υἱοθεσία) is put into those willing to believe, and no longer calling into slavery but into free dignity (ἀξίωμα). [Heading] Of the same, from the 4th tome of the (work) to the Corinthians, of Cyril. [Lemma] Slave were you called? Let it not concern you. Since some, deemed worthy of the grace of the Holy Spirit, were shaking off (ἀπεσείοντο) the yoke (ζυγός) of slavery according to flesh, he writes also through other (words) ‘Only not the freedom (ἐλευθερία) into occasion (ἀφορμή) for the flesh’, and he charms (καταγοητεύει) them as it were also through these, most elegantly (ἀστειότατα) saying ‘Slave were you called? Let it not concern you; but if also you are able to become free, rather use (χρῆσαι)’; that is, even if, having (the yoke) hung on you into the yoke of fleshly slavery, you were called through faith into free sonship (υἱότης), even if you have become partaker (κοινωνός) of divine nature, be better than small-souledness (μικροψυχία); you will find not unrewarded (ἄμισθον) the toil (πόνος) on slavery. For the creator (δημιουργός) knows the nature free; for it has been made so by him; but a certain greed (πλεονεξία), having run in beside (παρεισδραμοῦσα) somehow at times, ruined (διελυμήνατο) the beauty of freedom. It is needed by all means that those who suffered unload (ἀποφορτίσασθαι) the evil, (Christ) transforming (μεταστοιχειοῦντος) all things toward that in the beginnings, of Christ; for new creation (καινὴ κτίσις) the things in him, and neither slave nor free but all things and in all he. And indeed Isaiah, of the life expected and about to be, the state (κατάστασις) and the equality (ἰσότης) with God, cried out beforehand saying ‘And the people will be as the priest, and the servant (παῖς) as the master (κύριος), and the maidservant as the mistress.’ Therefore even if you could, he says, become free, rather use; for it is, as I said, not gainless (ἀκερδής) the yoke for those having used good will (εὔνοια) and having lived rightly in it; it will wrong (ἀδικήσει) the whole nothing that now from greed fleshly slavery has been thrown upon some; [ἔσται ἂν, sense: it will be/if] for all in equal manner and measure the free is preserved (σώζηται) with God who judges the just things and weighs (ταλαντεύοντι) our affairs holily. Otherwise also, he says, it would not be among possible things for us being humans to flee the name of slavery; for everything made is slave, and all that has been called into being (γένεσις) is subject to divine scepters (σκῆπτρα); so that also the slave is freedman (ἀπελεύθερος) of Christ, and slave by all means also the one called to freedom, as the psalm says ‘for all things are your slaves.’ The mystagogue (μυσταγωγός) shows also in another way those saved through him benefited (ὠφελουμένους) by Christ; so he says ‘With a price you were bought (ἠγοράσθητε), do not become slaves of men’; for we were bought with a price admittedly, the Savior of all of us Christ having laid down his own blood for us, we were taken out (ἐξῃρήμεθα) of the devil’s greed, of the demons’ cruelty (ὠμότης), we were called to freedom through Christ. Therefore as bought and owing their own life to the one who purchased (πριαμένῳ), do not become, he says, slaves of men. And we do not say that he persuades to leap off (ἀποπηδᾶν) from fleshly slavery, but rather he teaches that very rightly, not to serve (δουλεύειν) those who [try] to carry off (ἀποφέρειν) [continues in u03-rem-mid].
pass_b_english: …at times, though they had received the faith, they were seeking to be made complete in the flesh, just as some in Galatia did, whom the inspired Paul rebukes, saying, “Having begun in the Spirit, are you now being made complete in the flesh?” (Galatians 3:3).

So the way had to be opened wide for them by a clear and most vivid proclamation of the truth: that circumcision is nothing when it lacks the other commandments of God, and in the same way uncircumcision is nothing unless it is adorned with a life worthy of the Gospel (compare 1 Corinthians 7:19). It is fitting, then, that the one who has been called should remain in his calling, in whatever state he may be (compare 1 Corinthians 7:20).

He then passes, of necessity, to the need to drive off once more, as it were, another slander against the divine proclamation. For there was a spirit of slavery in those under the law; but the decree of the Gospel says that the Spirit of adoption is given to those who are willing to believe, and that it no longer calls them to slavery but to the dignity of the free (compare Romans 8:15).
By the same Cyril, from the fourth tome of his work on the Epistle to the Corinthians.

“Were you called as a slave? Do not let it trouble you” (1 Corinthians 7:21). Since some who had been counted worthy of the grace of the Holy Spirit were shaking off the yoke of slavery according to the flesh, he writes in another place too, “Only do not use your freedom as an opportunity for the flesh” (Galatians 5:13). Here also he wins them over, as it were, speaking with great grace: “Were you called as a slave? Do not let it trouble you; but even if you can become free, rather make use of it” (1 Corinthians 7:21).

That is: even if you were called through faith into free sonship while you still bore the yoke of slavery according to the flesh, even if you have become a partaker of the divine nature (2 Peter 1:4), rise above faint-heartedness; you will find that the toil you bear in slavery is not without its reward. For the Creator knows our nature as free, since it was made so by him; but a kind of greed, slipping in somehow over the course of time, has ruined the beauty of freedom.

Those who have suffered this must by all means throw off the burden of this evil, since Christ is refashioning all things to what they were in the beginning. For what is in him is a new creation (2 Corinthians 5:17), and there is neither slave nor free, but he himself is all and in all (Colossians 3:11). Indeed Isaiah cried out beforehand about the state of the life we await, the life that is to be, and about the equality that is found with God, saying, “And the people shall be as the priest, and the servant as his master, and the maidservant as her mistress” (Isaiah 24:2).

So, he says, even if you could become free, rather make use of it; for, as I said, the yoke is not without gain for those who have shown good will and have lived rightly under it. That slavery according to the flesh has now been laid on some out of greed will do no wrong at all, so long as freedom is kept for all alike, in equal manner and measure, before God, who judges what is just and weighs our affairs in holiness.

Besides, he says, since we are human beings, it is not possible for us to escape the name of slavery. For everything that has been made is a slave, and all that has been called into being is subject to the divine scepter. So the slave is Christ’s freedman, and the one called to freedom is surely a slave as well (compare 1 Corinthians 7:22), as the psalm says, “for all things are your slaves” (Psalm 119:91).

Yet the guide into the mysteries shows in another way too that those saved through Christ are helped by him. That is why he says, “You were bought with a price; do not become slaves of men” (1 Corinthians 7:23). For we were, beyond dispute, bought with a price, since Christ, the Savior of us all, paid his own blood for us; we have been rescued from the greed of the devil and from the cruelty of the demons, and we have been called to freedom through Christ (compare Galatians 5:13). So, as those who have been bought and who owe their own life to the One who purchased them, “do not become,” he says, “slaves of men.”
We do not say that he is urging them to leap out of slavery according to the flesh; rather he teaches this, and very rightly: not to be slaves to those who try to carry off…

Fixed in tr3.json. Wrong sense: ἀδικήσει δὲ τὸ σύμπαν οὐδέν is 'will do no wrong at all' (τὸ σύμπαν adverbial), not 'no harm to the whole'; ἔσται ἂν + subjunctive σώζηται is ἔστ' ἄν, 'so long as freedom is kept', not 'for freedom will be kept' (translator note updated). μέτεισι δὲ ἀναγκαίως ἐπὶ τὸ χρῆναι πάλιν … is 'he then passes, of necessity, to the need … once more', not 'from there he must go on' (modality and πάλιν). ἀποφορτίσασθαι τὸ κακόν is active middle, 'throw off the burden of this evil', not 'be relieved of'. τεθεικότος … τὸ ἴδιον αἷμα 'paid his own blood' fits the price image better than 'laid down his own blood'. PG heading reordered to 'By the same Cyril, from the fourth tome of his work …' (τοῦ αὐτοῦ … Κυρίλλου). House consistency with u03-open and the existing book rows: lower-case pronouns for God and Christ, 'the law' lower case, 'compare' on paraphrases and allusions (1 Corinthians 7:19, 7:20, 7:22; Romans 8:15; Galatians 5:13 second use). Scripture identifications verified (Galatians 3:3, 5:13; Isaiah 24:2 LXX; Psalm 119:91 = LXX 118:91; Colossians 3:11; 1 Corinthians 7:21, 7:23).
